subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth is a scholar with forty-one years in the West Inner Ward of Candlekeep, who navigates institutional gravity and knows which way to lean into it.
source_quote: Brother Vareth moves through it like a man who has been navigating institutional gravity for forty-one years and knows which way to lean into it.

subject: West Inner Ward
fact: The West Inner Ward smells like old paper, and the walls have absorbed it.
source_quote: The West Inner Ward smells like old paper. People here take themselves seriously, and the walls have absorbed it.

subject: Immortal Chambers
fact: The Immortal Chambers have a tile floor with one deity symbol per tile, and the problem is immediately apparent.
source_quote: The Immortal Chambers have a tile floor with one deity symbol per tile, and the problem is immediately apparent.

subject: Pizwog
fact: Pizwog is an ancient tortle who moves at the speed of an ancient tortle and distributes a religious tract that turns out to be one of his own research papers — a syncretic analysis of different religions across the Sword Coast.
source_quote: We are briefly interrupted by Pizwog, who is an ancient tortle and moves at the speed of an ancient tortle. I wait. He distributes what appears to be a religious tract, which turns out to be one of his own research papers — a syncretic analysis of different religions across the Sword Coast.

subject: Pizwog's research tract
fact: Pizwog's research tract is a syncretic analysis of different religions across the Sword Coast, deeply theoretical, internally inconsistent in ways the narrator can tell are meaningful, and written in the style of a man who has strong views about what the word *however* is for.
source_quote: a syncretic analysis of different religions across the Sword Coast, deeply theoretical, internally inconsistent in ways I can tell are meaningful without yet being able to specify how, and written in the style of a man who has strong views about what the word *however* is for.

subject: Sister Yvenne
fact: Sister Yvenne threatens to confiscate everyone's bookplates at Candlekeep.
source_quote: Sister Yvenne threatens to confiscate everyone's bookplates.

subject: Vareth's side office
fact: Vareth's side office is small and full, and he has been keeping this corner of the library for forty-one years.
source_quote: His side office is small and full. He has been keeping this corner of the library for forty-one years, he says, and he knows what a fashion looks like.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum proposes a fourth school of theological thought — the Grygum school — suggesting fixed points around which actions must revolve, with constraint near them and freedom between.
source_quote: But… but what if there's a fourth? What if there are certain fixed points around which our actions must revolve? And the closer we come to one of those fixed points, the more constrained we are, but between them, perhaps we have a great deal of freedom of action.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth names the Grygum school a compromise of the Bahamutian school and labels the narrator a weak Stroudite and a weak Bahamutian, calling it the strong-weak hypothesis.
source_quote: He calls it a compromise of the Bahamutian school. He calls me a weak Stroudite — a strong Stroudite holds there are no fixed points at all — and a strong Bahamutian around fixed points, and a weak Bahamutian outside of them. He names this the strong-weak hypothesis with the satisfaction of a man who has just filed something correctly.

subject: Stroudite papers
fact: Vareth hands the narrator a stack of Stroudite papers, barely able to contain himself, and rushes off to begin his own research.
source_quote: Then he hands me a stack of Stroudite papers, barely able to contain himself, and rushes off to begin his own research.

subject: Refectory
fact: The Refectory was built for scholars, with a ceiling high enough that a hill giant could sit comfortably at one end and not embarrass herself.
source_quote: The Refectory was built for scholars, which meant the ceiling was high enough that a hill giant could have sat comfortably at one end and not embarrassed herself.

subject: The Eight Great Readers
fact: The Eight Great Readers sit at the high table in the Refectory like they are posing for a tapestry.
source_quote: We found seats at a long table in the middle of the hall, away from the high table where the eight Great Readers sat like they were posing for a tapestry.

subject: Prophecies in the gallery
fact: Prophecies are recited from the gallery above the Refectory, originating from Alaundo, and are removed when fulfilled; what remains is the unfulfilled inventory.
source_quote: The prophecies had been going the whole time, floating down from the gallery above like water finding its level. Vareth had explained it to Grygum earlier in the day... there was a man named Alaundo whose prophecies had come true with uncomfortable regularity, so Candlekeep had been reciting them ever since. Whenever one came true, it was removed. What remained was the unfulfilled inventory.

subject: Prophecy: 'On the longest night of winter's deepest cold, the keeper falls, the heart is sold.'
fact: A prophecy recited from the gallery — 'On the longest night of winter's deepest cold, the keeper falls, the heart is sold.' — lands with the narrator and is kept silent.
source_quote: *On the longest night of winter's deepest cold, the keeper falls, the heart is sold.* It landed. I sat with it for a second.

subject: The hooded figure from the Avowed
fact: A hooded figure from the Avowed passes the dining hall at a half-run, something tucked against their ribs under the robe, not trying to be obvious but also not trying very hard not to be.
source_quote: And then a hooded figure from the Avowed went past the dining hall at a half-run, something tucked against their ribs under the robe. They weren't trying to be obvious about it. They also weren't trying very hard not to be.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, the grey ooze, had been confined to the bag of holding and is now done with it — he wants out.
source_quote: Glabbagool was in a state. The grey ooze had been confined to the bag of holding for most of the day... he was done with it. He wanted out.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is awakened by a messenger who says the Keeper of Tomes is dead, and the First Reader wants him through the emerald door before the Avowed awake.
source_quote: The knock came before the light did... Quick! The first reader sent me! The Keeper of Tomes is dead! She wants you! Now, through the emerald door, before the avowed awake!

subject: The Messenger
fact: The Messenger is commoner-born, enthusiastic, boyish, and looks like someone who sprinted across several corridors of very old stone and intended everyone to notice.
source_quote: He was commoner-born, I could see that much — enthusiastic in the way of someone who has been trusted with important information for the first time and found the experience clarifying. Boyish. Very slightly delighted by his own urgency, which I didn't hold against him. He looked like someone who had sprinted across several corridors of very old stone and intended everyone to notice.

subject: The Keeper of Tomes
fact: The Keeper of Tomes is dead, and her death has triggered an emergency summons to Daz and Grygum through the emerald door before the Avowed awake.
source_quote: The Keeper of Tomes is dead!

subject: The First Reader
fact: The First Reader bypasses standard channels to summon Daz and Grygum through the emerald door before the Avowed awake, indicating a desire to contain the scene before institutional management.
source_quote: The first reader sent me! ... She wants you! Now, through the emerald door, before the avowed awake!

subject: Emerald door
fact: The emerald door is the designated access point through which Daz and Grygum are summoned by the First Reader, bypassing standard institutional channels.
source_quote: Now, through the emerald door, before the avowed awake!

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum opens the door to the messenger and responds with a voice between inquiry and bracing for bad news: 'The Keeper of Tomes?'
source_quote: Grygum opened the door. I heard his voice land somewhere between inquiry and bracing for bad news: 'The Keeper of Tomes?'

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is set against the wall within reach in the hearth room — close but not drawn — as part of a long-standing negotiation with the narrator.
source_quote: I found a corner of the hearth room, set Dawnbringer against the wall within reach — close but not drawn, which had become its own negotiation over the weeks.

subject: Ilvara's prayer book
fact: Ilvara's prayer book is referenced by the narrator as part of a pattern of theological documents with hidden, conspiratorial intent — including Zuggtmoy marginalia and the Lolth/Zuggtmoy equivalence in Asha Vandree's chain mail.
source_quote: I think about Ilvara's prayer book. The Zuggtmoy marginalia. The theological document from Asha Vandree's chain mail — the Lolth/Zuggtmoy equivalence, written in a hand that wanted very much to seem incidental.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a place where three duels have been fought over which polemic shelf gets the larger window, despite no duels having occurred in two hundred years.
source_quote: Three duels have been fought at Candlekeep over which polemic shelf gets the larger window. *Three*, in a library where nobody has dueled in two hundred years.

subject: Protanther
fact: Protanther is referenced as an ancient dragon who honored Stroud's move because he is honorable, not because Bahamut compelled him.
source_quote: The Draconic school says ancient agency rules. Protanther honored Stroud's move because Protanther is honorable, not because Bahamut compelled him.

subject: Stroud
fact: Stroud is the great philosopher whose decisive move against a dragon who spent four hundred years studying that exact position is cited as an example of constrained choice within a fixed framework.
source_quote: I think about Stroud making the decisive move — the perfect throw, the unrepeatable instant — against a dragon who had spent four hundred years studying that exact position.

subject: Tiamat
fact: Tiamat was denied her power because a dwarf chose — cited by the Stroudite school as evidence of sovereign mortal choice.
source_quote: Tiamat was denied her power because a dwarf chose.

subject: Bahamut
fact: Bahamut is referenced as a deity whose divine providence prevails, moving pieces beforehand so mortals serve as instruments.
source_quote: The Bahamutian school says divine providence prevails. Bahamut moved his pieces beforehand.

subject: Zuggtmoy
fact: Zuggtmoy is referenced in marginalia and theological documents as a deity whose influence is subtly embedded in the architecture of belief, including the Lolth/Zuggtmoy equivalence.
source_quote: The Zuggtmoy marginalia. The theological document from Asha Vandree's chain mail — the Lolth/Zuggtmoy equivalence...

subject: Lolth
fact: Lolth is referenced in the theological document from Asha Vandree's chain mail as being equated with Zuggtmoy in a hand that wanted very much to seem incidental.
source_quote: The theological document from Asha Vandree's chain mail — the Lolth/Zuggtmoy equivalence, written in a hand that wanted very much to seem incidental.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is referenced as the owner of chain mail containing a theological document with the Lolth/Zuggtmoy equivalence written in a hand that wanted very much to seem incidental.
source_quote: The theological document from Asha Vandree's chain mail — the Lolth/Zuggtmoy equivalence, written in a hand that wanted very much to seem incidental.

subject: Alaundo
fact: Alaundo is the prophet whose prophecies have come true with uncomfortable regularity, leading Candlekeep to recite them continuously, removing them only when fulfilled.
source_quote: There was a man named Alaundo whose prophecies had come true with uncomfortable regularity, so Candlekeep had been reciting them ever since.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced as the one patiently teaching Glabbagool, the grey ooze, to formalize monastic discipline.
source_quote: Whatever Glabbagool had been doing in the bag all day — thinking, absorbing, trying to formalize whatever Zalthir had been patiently teaching him into monastic discipline...

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris knocks on Daz's door to deliver the news that the Keeper of Tomes is dead.
source_quote: The knock came before the light did... Fembris got through the second syllable...

subject: House of Rest
fact: The House of Rest is where Daz and Grygum return after the morning summons, and where Glabbagool is confined in the bag of holding.
source_quote: Back at the House of Rest, Glabbagool was in a state.

subject: Hearth room
fact: The hearth room is where Daz sits with Dawnbringer against the wall, the fire warm, and the prophecy echoing from the unseen gallery.
source_quote: I found a corner of the hearth room... The fire was going. The ceiling was still high enough. Above us, in a gallery I couldn't see, someone was still reciting.

subject: Underdark
fact: The Underdark is referenced as a place where patience is wrapped in the awareness that a tunnel can reverse on you while you're standing still, contrasting with Candlekeep's surface politics.
source_quote: The Underdark had bent that instinct a little — the patience was still there, but now it came wrapped in the awareness that a tunnel can reverse on you while you're standing still.

subject: The Grygum school
fact: The Grygum school of thought is a newly proposed theological framework suggesting fixed points around which actions must revolve, with constraint near them and freedom between — proposed by the narrator as an offhand remark and adopted by Vareth as the question of the age.
source_quote: The Grygum school of thought. Filed under: things that started as offhand remarks.

subject: The narrator
fact: The narrator proposes the Grygum school of thought by accident, tucks Pizwog's research tract into his satchel, and reflects on having handled the theological revelation competently.
source_quote: I feel like I handled that competently," I say, to no one in particular.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is referenced by the continuing speaker as the one who observed Glabbagool's assessment and noted the chamber's structural details, and who later questioned Bookwyrm's timing in volunteering information about Kalan's resignation.
source_quote: I watched him do it and thought: *at least we have that.*

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris is the guide who led the tour of the Bastion, described the Astronomicon and Drakonoikos, and named the Dragon Breath Simulation Chamber with warning tone.
source_quote: "Behold, the great library."

subject: Candlekeep's Bastion
fact: Candlekeep's Bastion contains three visible archways, one service passage, one guarded door to the north, oil paintings on every staircase, busts on pedestals at each landing, heavy tapestries, and the Drakonoikos structure built from enormous scales and bones.
source_quote: Exits: three visible archways, one service passage, one guarded door to the north. Foot traffic: light, scholars moving in pairs, nobody moving fast. No elevated positions. No obvious coverage points.

subject: Drakonoikos
fact: Drakonoikos is a structure built from enormous scales and bones worked into the walls, where the early light hits the scales and they hold it.
source_quote: The structure was built from scales — actual scales, enormous, overlapping — and bones worked into the walls where another building would have used stone.

subject: Astronomicon
fact: Astronomicon is a stack of blue globes ascending in scale, pale against the white sky, said to contain everything known about the stars.
source_quote: A stack of blue globes, ascending in scale, pale against the white sky.

subject: Dragon Breath Simulation Chamber
fact: Dragon Breath Simulation Chamber is a chamber inside the Bastion where one of the Avowed died, requiring the Keeper's permission for access.
source_quote: One of the Avowed had died in it, he said, which was why the Keeper's permission was now required.

subject: Chapter House
fact: Chapter House contains twelve chairs around a twelve-sided table, a rose window throwing colored light across the stone floor, and western gables pressing down overhead.
source_quote: The Chapter House was exactly as described — twelve chairs around a twelve-sided table, rose window throwing colored light across the stone floor, western gables pressing down overhead like a building that took itself seriously.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is the green dragonborn who proposed delegating the investigation to the party, offered vague but workable remuneration terms, and revealed that Janussi had asked Kalan to resign before his death.
source_quote: "Let's be calm ourselves…"

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is the gate warden with a gray-white beard and piercing blue eyes, who was asked to resign by Janussi and later entered the Chapter House after the council's decision.
source_quote: Then Kalan Strongbranch walked in.

subject: A'lai Aivenmore
fact: A'lai Aivenmore is the tall, handsome council member with a braided beard who advocated for restoring leadership to Candlekeep and decided the fastest resolution was best.
source_quote: "We must have the vote and restore leadership to Candlekeep."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is the speaker who introduced himself as founder of the Grygumite School, negotiated remuneration for the investigation, and referenced Poirot and Colombo.
source_quote: "I am the head of the Grygumite School. Founder, in fact."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the speaker who proposed remuneration in books, referenced Poirot and Colombo, and insisted on carte blanche access to the library.
source_quote: "Are we supposed to investigate if we can't poke around?"

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the one who noted Bookwyrm’s timing in volunteering information about Kalan’s resignation and asked what type of work Kalan was negligent in.
source_quote: What type of work was he negligent in?

subject: Candlekeep's Library
fact: Candlekeep's Library is a place where books are copied at the House of the Binder upon successful completion of an investigation, and where full access is requested but initially withheld.
source_quote: One book each, copied at the House of the Binder, upon successful completion.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sword housed in its scabbard that claimed to have been found in a tomb after two thousand years.
source_quote: Dawnbringer, housed in her scabbard, took the opportunity to note that we must surely be the greatest discoverers of all, having found her tomb after two thousand years.

subject: Janussi's Death
fact: Janussi, the Keeper of Tomes, was found dead, and on the morning of his death, he had asked Kalan Strongbranch to tender his resignation due to concerns about mental faculties and negligence.
source_quote: Janussi, the morning before his death, had asked Kalan to tender his resignation. Mental faculties. Negligence.

subject: Investigation Delegation
fact: The Council of Twelve delegated the investigation of Janussi's death to the party, citing fate and divine intervention, and agreed to provide one book each upon successful completion.
source_quote: "seekers who the gods have sent us"

subject: Remuneration Negotiation
fact: The party negotiated for remuneration in the form of one book each from the library, and demanded full access to the library as a condition of the investigation.
source_quote: "We need an all-access library card."

subject: House of the Binder
fact: House of the Binder is the location where books are copied for the party upon successful completion of the investigation.
source_quote: One book each, copied at the House of the Binder, upon successful completion.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is the one who revealed that Janussi had asked Kalan to resign and later stated, "I had nothing to do with it," when asked where she was.
source_quote: "I can assure you, I had nothing to do with it."

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the one who noted that Bookwyrm’s volunteered information about Kalan’s resignation was given before anyone asked, and who later questioned the nature of Kalan’s negligence.
source_quote: I filed that immediately — not the content, the timing.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz says, 'Investigating,' I said, keeping my voice even, 'part of investigating is getting input from everybody we talk to.'
source_quote: I don't want to prejudice your investigation. I'm sure if you examine the evidence—

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin says, 'But your testimony is evidence.' A beat. 'Maybe you are evidence, and we should examine you.'
source_quote: No, no, I don't want to prejudice! I'm sure if you examine the evidence.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm says, 'Nobody had been able to conclusively prove the cat was some kind of power that lived here, and nobody had been able to conclusively prove that it was not.'
source_quote: nobody had been able to conclusively prove the cat was some kind of power that lived here, and nobody had been able to conclusively prove that it was not

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris says, 'These Avowed had taken a cat sitting wherever it liked and turned it into an interstellar, interspatial, interdimensional horror — that's just what cats do.'
source_quote: these Avowed had taken a cat sitting wherever it liked and turned it into an interstellar, interspatial, interdimensional horror — that's just what cats do

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir says, very quietly, 'Is it?'
source_quote: Is it?

subject: Tadric
fact: Tadric says, 'My assignment had been crowd control. Not observation.'
source_quote: My assignment had been crowd control. Not observation.

subject: Tadric
fact: Tadric says, 'Kalan looked more determined coming out than going in.'
source_quote: Kalan looked more determined coming out than going in.

subject: Tadric
fact: Tadric says, 'The dead had not spoken.'
source_quote: The dead had not spoken.

subject: Tadric
fact: Tadric says, 'Miss Hollypocket would never have allowed the Keeper to let candles burn down to nothing.'
source_quote: Miss Hollypocket would never have allowed the Keeper to let candles burn down to nothing.

subject: tower interior
fact: The staircase spiraled up through the tower's interior — reception chamber at the first landing, a shrine of Oghma at the second, a large apartment at the third with its door left conspicuously ajar.
source_quote: The staircase spiraled up through the tower's interior — reception chamber at the first landing, a shrine of Oghma at the second, a large apartment at the third with its door left conspicuously ajar.

subject: Keeper's Chambers
fact: The room was circular, ringed with lancet windows, full of pale morning light that had gone slightly yellow and hazy from something I placed almost immediately: tobacco smoke. Lingering. The windows were shut.
source_quote: The room was circular, ringed with lancet windows, full of pale morning light that had gone slightly yellow and hazy from something I placed almost immediately: tobacco smoke. Lingering. The windows were shut.

subject: Keeper's Chambers
fact: The safe on the far wall had been opened. Blue gems and empty pouches scattered on the floor in front of it.
source_quote: The safe on the far wall had been opened. Blue gems and empty pouches scattered on the floor in front of it.

subject: Keeper's Chambers
fact: The desk was neatly kept, which was itself a data point. The chair near it was toppled. The marble statue and its pedestal were on the floor. The candelabra — seven arms, bronze — had burned its candles entirely to wax puddles.
source_quote: The desk was neatly kept, which was itself a data point. The chair near it was toppled. The marble statue and its pedestal were on the floor. The candelabra — seven arms, bronze — had burned its candles entirely to wax puddles.

subject: spellbook
fact: A spellbook sat open in the center of the desk: The Discoveries.
source_quote: A spellbook sat open in the center of the desk: The Discoveries.

subject: notes
fact: To one side, notes in Celestial, generic academic work, someone musing on unfamiliar workings and how they might be performed.
source_quote: To one side, notes in Celestial, generic academic work, someone musing on unfamiliar workings and how they might be performed.

subject: notes
fact: To the other side, a larger pile of notes pinned under a quartz weight, with more annotations on top in midnight blue ink — and below those, older notes in purple.
source_quote: To the other side, a larger pile of notes pinned under a quartz weight, with more annotations on top in midnight blue ink — and below those, older notes in purple.

subject: quill
fact: A quill on the floor. Nib covered in midnight blue.
source_quote: A quill on the floor. Nib covered in midnight blue.

subject: ink carrier
fact: A wicker basket nearby holding a linen ink carrier, slightly damp, which had been the vessel for the ink now pooling from the spilled pot.
source_quote: A wicker basket nearby holding a linen ink carrier, slightly damp, which had been the vessel for the ink now pooling from the spilled pot.

subject: The Golden Ass
fact: The book the blue ink was annotating — The Golden Ass — wasn't in the room.
source_quote: The book the blue ink was annotating — The Golden Ass — wasn't in the room.

subject: candelabra
fact: The candelabra — seven arms, bronze — had burned its candles entirely to wax puddles.
source_quote: The candelabra — seven arms, bronze — had burned its candles entirely to wax puddles.

subject: gate warden's inspection
fact: The Gate Warden returned at eleven, alone, for a full inspection — careful, deliberate, left to make his report to the Council.
source_quote: The Gate Warden again at eleven, alone, for a full inspection — careful, deliberate, left to make his report to the Council.

subject: death of Janussi
fact: Janussi was found dead by the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore and the housekeeper, one Miss Hollypocket, around half past seven in the morning.
source_quote: Janussi found dead by the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore and the housekeeper, one Miss Hollypocket, around half past seven in the morning.

subject: ritual attempt on corpse
fact: The dead had not spoken. Someone — presumably the Gate Warden, before his removal — had already used the rite on the corpse, which meant we'd be waiting if we wanted to try again.
source_quote: The dead had not spoken. Someone — presumably the Gate Warden, before his removal — had already used the rite on the corpse, which meant we'd be waiting if we wanted to try again.

subject: candle burning
fact: The candles told the same story. I said it out loud: 'That tells me that it had been some time since he was murdered, because there was enough time for the candle to burn out.'
source_quote: The candles told the same story. I said it out loud: 'That tells me that it had been some time since he was murdered, because there was enough time for the candle to burn out.'

subject: rib cage damage
fact: The rib cage had been smashed by something like an axe, multiple blows, close together, deliberate. The heart was missing. No other organs.
source_quote: The rib cage had been smashed by something like an axe, multiple blows, close together, deliberate. The heart was missing. No other organs.

subject: heart removal
fact: The missing heart wasn't the cause of death. It was a message. Or a precaution.
source_quote: The missing heart wasn't the cause of death. It was a message. Or a precaution.

subject: resurrection prevention
fact: You can't bring someone back from death by ritual if their vital organs aren't present. Whoever took the heart wasn't souvenir-collecting. They were preventing resurrection.
source_quote: You can't bring someone back from death by ritual if their vital organs aren't present. Whoever took the heart wasn't souvenir-collecting. They were preventing resurrection.

subject: door left ajar
fact: A door left ajar on the third floor landing.
source_quote: A door left ajar on the third floor landing.

subject: Bookwyrm's instructions
fact: The Bookwyrm's parting instructions had been clear enough: report back when done, remove nothing from the room.
source_quote: report back when done, remove nothing from the room

subject: cat
fact: Gray. Motionless. Yellow eyes that opened the moment we got close. The cat had decided it need not move for anyone, and tracked us anyway.
source_quote: Gray. Motionless. Yellow eyes that opened the moment we got close. The cat had decided it need not move for anyone, and tracked us anyway.

subject: third floor apartment
fact: A large apartment at the third with its door left conspicuously ajar.
source_quote: A large apartment at the third with its door left conspicuously ajar.
